title: Opportunistically determined bone mineral density: "Comparison of QCT-based bone mineral density with opportunistically determined bone mineral density in the spine"
summary: Osteoporosis is a common condition in the population and frequently leads to vertebral body fractures. In order to prevent the occurrence of vertebral body fractures and, if necessary, to be able to initiate drug therapy in good time, it is necessary to measure bone mineral density. The common method for this is currently DXA and QCT. The present study aims to investigate the extent to which modern opportunistic, algorithm-based measurement methods provide reliable results for the determination of bone mineral density. Thus, it will be investigated whether these methods can be established in clinical routine in the future.

interventions.name: Patients with and without osteoporotic vertebral fracture who received CT of the spine and QCT for bone mineral densitometry as part of routine clinical practice (coverage period 2000-2022).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. QCT and routine CT of the spine present
2. maximum time interval between QCT and routine CT of 30 days
3. all underlying diseases except multiple myeloma
4. at least one vertebral body from BWK 12 to LWK 4 present and measurable by both QCT and routine CT (i.e., no fracture, no foreign material/cement within the vertebral body)
5. for routine CT, either the raw data set (axial with max. slice thickness of 1 mm) and/or a sagittal reconstruction of the spine bony is available (sagittal with max. slice thickness of 3 mm)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Age under 18 years
2. Incomplete examination data
